title: Invitation flow metadata can link parent, child account, and invited guardian
description: Even if payload contents are protected, the fact that this invitation flow occurs can reveal an association between the parent account, the child's account or profile, and the invited guardian's identifier. Such metadata may enable linking of family relationships across records or sessions.
assumptions: Assumes network, application, or service metadata exposes sender/recipient/account correlation beyond strictly necessary processing.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may be approximate; threat is primarily about linkability via flow metadata.

title: Invitation request may identify the invited guardian or child-related context in transit metadata
description: Identifiers in the request or its metadata may allow an observer or intermediary with access to logs, headers, URLs, or message traces to identify the invited guardian, the parent account, or infer that the invitation concerns a specific child-location-sharing service.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers may appear in transport/application metadata or insufficiently protected logs.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate from memory.

title: Backend stores invitation details more broadly than necessary
description: On receipt, the backend may retain invitation payloads, contact details, relationship information, or audit records in logs or databases accessible to internal staff or other components, causing unnecessary disclosure of the invited guardian's and family's personal data.
assumptions: Assumes backend persistence, logging, or internal sharing of invitation data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact subtree may differ.

title: Backend may process invitation data for purposes not expected by the parent or invited guardian
description: The backend could use invitation data for analytics, growth metrics, contact graph building, or future outreach beyond the immediate purpose of enabling guardian access. This creates a risk that data is used in ways not transparent to the individuals involved.
assumptions: Assumes invitation data is available for secondary processing beyond access provisioning.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ; threat is clearly one of unawareness/unexpected processing.

title: Insufficient consent or legal basis management for inviting another guardian
description: The backend may accept and process an invitation without ensuring that the invited guardian has been properly informed or that any required consent, parental authority, or other legal basis checks are satisfied before their personal data is processed.
assumptions: Assumes the service is responsible for enforcing or evidencing consent/legal-basis requirements for invited adults' data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact non-compliance subtree may differ.

title: Backend may lack adequate evidence of who initiated the invitation and under what notice
description: If the backend does not keep reliable records of the parent's invitation action, notices shown, and the data submitted, it may be difficult to demonstrate whether the invitation was legitimately initiated or whether proper privacy notices and choices were presented. This can undermine accountability and enable repudiation of the sharing action.
assumptions: Assumes auditability is relevant for privacy accountability in this feature.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; mapping of repudiation in LINDDUN Pro may vary.

title: Backend discloses child's live location to a secondary guardian without valid authorization or consent
description: The backend's act of granting access and sharing the child's live location may disclose highly sensitive real-time location data to EE3 without a valid legal basis, parental authorization, or the child's/primary guardian's informed consent. Because the source decides to release the data, the disclosure threat arises at P1.
assumptions: Assumes access rights for the secondary guardian may be misconfigured, stale, overly broad, or granted without robust verification of relationship and purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for unauthorized disclosure by the sender; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree numbering may differ.

title: Backend uses location data for a new recipient/purpose beyond the user's expectations
description: Sharing live location with a secondary guardian may be incompatible with the purpose originally understood by the child or primary guardian, especially if they expected location sharing only with the primary guardian or only for emergency use. The backend's decision to extend access can therefore create an unawareness threat.
assumptions: Assumes notices, consent flows, or in-app explanations do not clearly explain ongoing sharing with secondary guardians.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort fit for insufficient user awareness/transparency about processing purposes and recipients.

title: Live location data in transit can directly identify the child and associated guardian relationship
description: The data flow contains real-time location information and likely account or session context tying the location to a specific child and secondary guardian. Interception or observation of the flow could therefore identify the child and reveal that EE3 is connected to that child.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted payload or accompanying metadata contains identifiers, tokens, device IDs, account references, or other context linking the location to a specific individual.

title: Transmission metadata can link child, backend account, and secondary guardian
description: Even if payload contents are protected, traffic metadata such as endpoints, timing, frequency, account references, or notification patterns may allow an observer to link the child to EE3 and infer an ongoing guardianship or caregiving relationship.
assumptions: Assumes some observable metadata exists to network observers, service operators, or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via communication metadata on the flow.

title: Secondary guardian may further disclose or expose the child's live location
description: Once EE3 receives the child's live location, they may intentionally or accidentally share it onward, expose it on an insecure device, or allow others nearby to view it. This creates an additional disclosure threat at the destination because it arises from the recipient's handling of the data.
assumptions: Assumes EE3 may use shared devices, screenshots, insecure storage, or onward communications outside the original sharing context.

title: Secondary guardian can link repeated live-location updates into movement patterns
description: By receiving continuous or repeated live-location updates, EE3 can link multiple observations over time to build a detailed pattern of the child's routines, school attendance, home location, and social activities.

title: Secondary guardian can infer sensitive information from the child's live location
description: The recipient can derive sensitive facts from the child's location, such as home address, school, religious attendance, medical visits, or visits to other sensitive venues. This is a detectability/disclosure-style privacy harm caused by processing at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes location precision and update frequency are sufficient to infer sensitive places or habits.

title: Secondary guardian may be unable to demonstrate or honor the agreed confidentiality constraints
description: If there are policy or consent constraints on when and how the child's location may be accessed or shared, EE3 may not be contractually or technically bound to comply, making it difficult to enforce or demonstrate compliance with those constraints at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes the system lacks enforceable downstream usage controls, auditability, or explicit obligations on EE3.

title: Shared analytics may enable cross-context linkage by the partner
description: Even if the backend shares only aggregated usage and engagement analytics, the chosen aggregation dimensions, cohort sizes, timestamps, campaign identifiers, app version, region, or other quasi-identifiers may allow the advertising/analytics partner to link this dataset with other datasets it already holds, connecting app audiences or small cohorts across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the partner receives breakdowns by dimensions or time windows rather than only very coarse global totals.

title: Aggregated analytics may still permit inference about users or small groups
description: Aggregation does not necessarily prevent identifiability. Small cohort counts, sparse segments, or repeated reports over time can let the recipient infer information about particular users or narrowly defined groups, especially when combined with external data.
assumptions: Assumes some reports may involve low-count segments or repeated segmented disclosures.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from insufficiently aggregated or segment-level analytics; exact node id may vary.

title: Sharing analytics with a third-party partner may disclose behavioral information beyond user expectations
description: Usage and engagement analytics reveal behavioral patterns about how people use the app. Sending these analytics to an external advertising/analytics partner discloses personal or group behavioral information to a third party, potentially beyond what users expect from a free-tier funding model.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics reflect user behavior and are not purely operational metrics with no user-related content.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for third-party sharing of behavioral analytics; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Partner may combine received analytics with its broader ecosystem data
description: On receipt, the advertising/analytics partner may correlate the app's analytics with data from other apps, websites, devices, or campaigns in its ecosystem, increasing linkability of audiences, cohorts, or potentially individuals.

uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side linkage through dataset combination; exact node id may differ.

description: The recipient may use auxiliary information, historical reports, or fine-grained segmentation to infer the presence, behavior, or attributes of specific users despite the data being described as aggregated.

uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side identifiability/re-identification from received analytics; exact node id may differ.

title: Partner may use analytics for secondary purposes

description: If the sharing is not clearly communicated, users may not understand that their usage and engagement data contributes to analytics sent to an external partner to fund the free tier, undermining transparency.

uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact node id may differ.

title: Third-party analytics sharing may be incompatible with user consent or stated purpose
description: Sharing app usage analytics with an advertising/analytics partner may exceed the purpose users reasonably expect, or may occur without valid consent or another appropriate legal basis, especially where analytics support advertising-related monetization.

This enables building a longitudinal picture of the child's movements, habits, and emergency behavior.

title: Disclosure of sensitive communication metadata in transit
description: The existence, timing, frequency, and endpoints of SOS/check-in messages can reveal that a child is traveling, away from expected places, or experiencing a potentially urgent event, even aside from the message content itself. title: Backend can expose or overuse stored location/SOS data
description: Once received, the backend may store, analyze, or internally share the child's location and SOS history beyond what is necessary to notify the parent. This can disclose sensitive patterns such as home, school, routines, and incidents of distress to operators, other systems, or unauthorized parties if access controls or minimization are insufficient.

title: Secondary use of SOS/location data beyond emergency notification
description: The backend may use the child's check-in/SOS and location data for analytics, profiling, product improvement, safety scoring, or other purposes not expected in the immediate act of alerting the parent. Such use can be incompatible with the original emergency/check-in purpose.

description: Processing may be non-compliant if the service lacks valid consent/authorization, age-appropriate transparency, or another lawful basis for collecting and handling a child's precise location and distress-related message. Children's data generally requires heightened safeguards and clear notice.

This can undermine accountability around a sensitive event.
